svg.title: Skewed chair envelope and bounded model support
svg.desc: Three synthetic support-calculation cases in model millimetres, not captured FreeCAD output. The timber length axis is y and width axis is x. In the first case its centre is (0,0), width 4 and length 30. The chair support C=(0.6,0), intended rail tangent (4/5,-3/5), outward axis (3/5,4/5), gauge normal (-3/5,-4/5) and local y axis (-4/5,3/5) are explicit. At the retained source's scale 1:76.2 and fixed 0.90 mm rail head width, source-labelled code 1 has local support-rectangle x limits -11/5 and 79/30 and y limits plus/minus 4/3. Its transformed corners are (26/75,-64/25), (487/150,98/75), (167/150,218/75), and (-134/75,-24/25). With both automatic-support settings true, margin 0.15 and per-side limit 2, its approach extension is zero and exit need 419/300 rounds upwards to 1.40 in 0.05 mm steps. Effective width becomes 5.40 at centre (0.70,0); edges are x=-2 and x=3.4. Exit clearance becomes 23/150, approximately 0.153 mm. The first drawing crops the 30 mm timber to its centre; end stations remain y=plus/minus 15. The pale rounded base is a schematic symbol; the dashed polygon is the separate support rectangle used for the arithmetic. Both drawings use equal x/y scale at 42 pixels/mm. In case 2 the chair and its intended rail move together to C=(1.25,0). Exit need 307/150 rounds to 2.05, above the 2 mm limit, so no side extension applies; source inspection predicts blocked support metadata with no new layout or chair solid. Case 3 restores C=(0.6,0) and shortens the timber to 5.50 mm. Side widening still passes, but far-end clearance remains -47/300, approximately -0.157 mm. The source can create a failed 2D layout with two critical findings for this one overhanging chair and red chair-envelope and effective-timber outlines. All three cases are independently checked rational arithmetic and source-inspected paths, not complete turnout recipes, GUI test results or evidence of physical fit or production readiness.

g.text: Centre crop; ends stay at y = ±15

for the chair rectangle and its timber.
x → timber width · y ↑ timber length
